Q0594

“God has given us the Torah and also intellect, so that we…” — Saadia Gaon (The Book of Beliefs and Opinions,…)

Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to The Book of Beliefs and Opinions, Introduction (Rosenblatt) and files it under Jewish Rationalism. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Saadia Gaon

Saadia ben Joseph (882–942), gaon of Sura, wrote The Book of Beliefs and Opinions, the first systematic Jewish philosophical theology in the Islamic world. He defended rabbinic Judaism against Karaites and used Arabic kalām methods to show that Torah and intellect agree when both are rightly understood.

How to read this passage

Philosophers disagree about whether reason is the slave of the passions, the legislator of morality, or one tool among others. The quotations here keep that disagreement in play. This passage enters that discussion through reason, faith.

Concepts in this quote

Reason
Reason is the capacity to give and assess reasons—central to logic, science, ethics, and public argument.
Faith
Faith appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat faith as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.
